question.text: An insulated copper wire of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn></math> turns is wrapped around a wooden cylindrical core of the cross-sectional area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>24</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. The two ends of the wire are connected to a resistor. The total resistance in the circuit is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>. If an externally applied uniform magnetic field in the core along its axis changes from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> in one direction to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> in the opposite direction, the charge flowing through a point in the circuit during the change of magnetic field will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mC</mi></math>.

solution.text:
The induced emf ε in the turns of the coil can be written as

ε=-dφdt=iR   ...1

Simplify equation (1) to obtain the required charge through a point in the circuit.

-dφdt=iR⇒-1R∫φ1φ2dφ=∫idt⇒q=φ1-φ2R   ...2

Where, φ1, φ2 are the magnetic flux associated with the coil from two ends.

As, φ=NBA, from equation (2), it can be written that

q=NARB1-B2   ...3

where, N, A are the number of turns and the cross-sectional area of the core respectively.

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required charge.

q=100×24×10-4 m2×1.5 T--1.5 T12 Ω=0.06 C×1000 mC1 C= 60 mC
